Background task initializes ChalDilliEnhanced instance
Chat endpoint receives query, calls get_delhi_response in thread pool with timeout

Returns formatted responses with Hinglish text and structured data

ParseBot API key exposed in code
No rate limiting on public endpoints

files.purpose: Core orchestration module that coordinates all subsystems (metro routing, food recommendations, bus routing, events, small-talk). Detects query intent and routes to appropriate handler. Integrates real-time data from scrapers.
inputs: Natural language query strings in English/Hindi/Hinglish
outputs: Structured response dict with text, recommendations, metadata
core_steps: Initialize all subsystems (metro router, food recommender, DTC router, conversation manager)
Detect query intent (metro, bus, food, events, attractions, small-talk)
Route to appropriate handler based on intent
For metro queries: extract route, get GTFS-based routing, optionally add food recommendations at destination
For food queries: extract area, get location-based recommendations
For bus queries: extract route, use DTC GTFS router
Format response in detected language (Hindi/Hinglish/English)
potential_risks: Intent misclassification (food vs metro queries)
GTFS data may be outdated
Food data CSV may have stale restaurant info
No caching of frequent queries
DTC router may fail if GTFS missing

files.purpose: Low-level metro routing engine using GTFS data. Implements Dijkstra algorithm for shortest path finding with transfer penalties. Handles station name matching, fare estimation, and route segmentation by line.
inputs: GTFS directory path with stops.txt, routes.txt, trips.txt, stop_times.txt
outputs: Route dictionary with segments, duration, distance, fare estimate
core_steps: Load GTFS files (stops, routes, trips, stop_times)
Build graph adjacency list from trip sequences
Calculate edge weights using haversine distance
Normalize and match station names using fuzzy matching with Jaccard similarity
Run Dijkstra algorithm with transfer penalties (7 min per transfer)
Segment path by route_id to identify line changes
Estimate fare based on distance slabs and Airport Express usage
Format human-readable route with line names and station sequences
potential_risks: GTFS data format changes break parsing
Station name matching may fail for uncommon names
Fare estimation is approximate (not real-time)
No real-time service disruptions considered
Graph building is memory-intensive for large networks

files.purpose: High-level metro routing wrapper that adds language detection, query parsing, station aliases, and gate information. Provides dual route options (low-fare vs fastest) and formats responses in user's language.
outputs: Formatted route response in detected language
core_steps: Detect language (Hindi/Hinglish/English) from query text
Extract source and destination using regex patterns
Normalize station names using alias mapping
Call MetroRouter for primary route (low-fare preference with Airport Express penalty)
Call MetroRouter for alternative route (fastest, no penalty)
Format both routes in detected language
Add gate information for source and destination stations
Return structured response with route data
potential_metrics: user preference for low-fare vs fastest
potential_risks: Regex patterns may miss edge cases in query format
Station aliases may not cover all variations
Gate data may be incomplete
Language detection may misclassify mixed queries

files.purpose: DTC bus routing engine using GTFS data. Similar to metro router but optimized for bus networks with different speed parameters and transfer penalties. Provides bus route planning between stops.
inputs: GTFS directory with bus data (stops.csv, routes.csv, trips.csv, stop_times.csv)
outputs: Bus route with segments, duration, distance
core_steps: Load bus GTFS files
Build graph from trip sequences
Match stop names using fuzzy matching
Run Dijkstra with bus-specific parameters (25 km/h speed, 5 min transfer penalty)
Segment path by route to show bus transfers
Format human-readable route with bus route names and stop sequences
potential_risks: Bus GTFS data may be less accurate than metro
Stop names may have more variations
No real-time bus arrival data
Transfer penalties may not reflect actual wait times

files.purpose: Location-based restaurant recommendation system. Uses CSV data as primary source, falls back to OSM when needed. Provides two recommendations per query: safe_pick (highest rating) and local_favourite (most reviews).
outputs: Dictionary with safe_pick and local_favourite recommendations
Restaurant data with ratings, cost, distance, Zomato links
core_steps: Load and preprocess food_data.csv on import
Build area index for fuzzy area name matching
For coordinate queries: filter restaurants within radius using haversine distance
If CSV results < 3: reverse geocode to get area, filter CSV by area, fallback to OSM if still empty
Rank candidates: safe_pick = highest rating (tie-break: rating_count, distance), local_favourite = highest rating_count (tie-break: rating, distance)
Format recommendations with exact field list (name, area, rating, cost_for_two, zomato_url, etc.)
potential_risks: Food data CSV may have stale restaurant info
OSM data quality varies by location
No real-time restaurant availability
Area name matching may fail for new areas
Haversine distance doesn't account for actual travel routes

files.purpose: Provides accessible gate and lift information for DMRC metro stations. Loads data from dmrc_gates.csv and uses fuzzy matching to find best gate recommendations for Divyangjan (persons with disabilities).
outputs: Gate information dictionary with gate number, lift availability, exit landmark
Formatted gate suggestion text in multiple languages
core_steps: Load dmrc_gates.csv on import
Normalize station name (remove 'metro station', 'stn' suffixes)
Fuzzy match station name against CSV data using SequenceMatcher
Score gates: prefer entries with lift availability, then lower gate numbers
Format suggestion text in detected language (Hindi/Hinglish/English) with landmark info
potential_risks: Gate data CSV may be incomplete
Fuzzy matching may return wrong station
Gate information may be outdated
No validation of gate data quality

files.purpose: Small-talk handler using HuggingFace Hinglish conversation dataset. Builds TF-IDF index for similarity matching and returns contextually appropriate replies for casual queries.
outputs: Best matching reply text from dataset
core_steps: Load dataset from HuggingFace or fallback to cached CSV
Sample up to max_rows (30000) entries randomly
Build TF-IDF vectorizer with n-gram range (1,2)
Transform all inputs to TF-IDF matrix
For query: transform to vector, compute cosine similarity with all entries
Return best match if similarity >= threshold (0.18)
potential_risks: HuggingFace dataset download may fail
TF-IDF index is memory-intensive
Similarity threshold may be too low/high
Dataset may not cover all query types

end_to_end_flows.name: Metro Routing Flow
end_to_end_flows.entry_point: User types metro route query in frontend chat box (e.g., 'dwarka se kashmere gate kaise jaana hai')
end_to_end_flows.description: User submits a metro route query in Hinglish or English. Frontend sends POST request to /chat endpoint. API server calls ChalDilliEnhanced.get_delhi_response which detects metro intent using keyword patterns and route extraction. EnhancedMetroRouter extracts source/destination using regex, normalizes station names with aliases, and detects language. MetroRouter loads GTFS data, builds graph, matches stations using fuzzy matching, runs Dijkstra algorithm with transfer penalties, segments route by line, estimates fare, and formats human-readable route. Gate lookup adds accessibility information for source/destination stations. Response is formatted in detected language and returned to frontend for display.

end_to_end_flows.name: DTC Routing Flow
end_to_end_flows.entry_point: User types DTC bus route query (e.g., 'dtc bus route from dwarka to kashmere gate')
end_to_end_flows.description: User submits a DTC bus route query. Frontend sends POST to /chat. ChalDilliEnhanced detects bus intent using explicit bus keywords ('dtc', 'bus', 'bus route'). Extracts source and destination from query using regex patterns. Calls DTCRouter.get_route which loads bus GTFS data, builds graph from trip sequences, matches stop names using fuzzy matching, runs Dijkstra with bus-specific parameters (25 km/h speed, 5 min transfer penalty), segments path by route to show bus transfers, and formats human-readable route. Response includes duration, distance, and step-by-step bus route with transfer points. Formatted in Hinglish style and returned to frontend.

end_to_end_flows.name: Food Recommendation Flow
end_to_end_flows.entry_point: User types food query (e.g., 'food recommendations in rohini' or 'momos near dwarka')
end_to_end_flows.description: User submits a food query mentioning area or coordinates. Frontend sends POST to /chat. ChalDilliEnhanced detects food intent using keywords ('food', 'eat', 'restaurant', 'momos', etc.). Extracts area name from query using area_mapper which checks for 'near', 'in', 'around' patterns and matches against hardcoded Delhi area dictionary. Food recommender loads food_data.csv, filters restaurants by area or calculates haversine distance for coordinate queries. If CSV results < 3, reverse geocodes coordinates to get area name and filters CSV by area. If still empty, falls back to OSM Overpass API. Ranks candidates: safe_pick = highest rating, local_favourite = highest rating_count. Formats recommendations with name, area, rating, cost_for_two, zomato_url. Response includes formatted text and structured recommendations dict. Frontend displays text and renders clickable Zomato links for both recommendations.

end_to_end_flows.name: Event Discovery Flow
end_to_end_flows.entry_point: User types event query (e.g., 'what events are happening' or frontend calls ParseBot endpoint)
end_to_end_flows.description: For general event queries, ChalDilliEnhanced calls get_event_response which uses data_scraper to fetch events from RSS feeds (BookMyShow, Eventbrite, Zomato) or returns fallback sample events. For specific event page URLs, frontend or external service calls POST /api/parse-events-from-url with URL. ParseBot wrapper launches Playwright headless browser, navigates to URL, waits for page load, extracts fully rendered HTML (including JavaScript content), sends HTML to Parse.bot API parse_events_from_html endpoint, and returns parsed events JSON. Response includes event title, date, venue, description. Events are formatted and displayed in frontend. Technical events use separate endpoint /api/parse-technical-events which sends URL directly to Parse.bot without Playwright.

end_to_end_flows.name: Small-Talk Conversation Flow
end_to_end_flows.entry_point: User types casual query that doesn't match metro, bus, food, or events (e.g., 'kaise ho', 'kya chal raha')
end_to_end_flows.description: User submits a casual query that doesn't match any specific intent. ChalDilliEnhanced falls back to HinglishConversationManager which loads Hinglish conversation dataset from HuggingFace (or cached CSV). Builds TF-IDF vectorizer with n-gram range (1,2), transforms all dataset inputs to TF-IDF matrix. For query, transforms to vector, computes cosine similarity with all entries, returns best match if similarity >= 0.18 threshold. Reply is returned as plain text response. If no match found or similarity too low, returns generic unknown response. This provides natural small-talk capability for casual Delhi-related conversations.
